title: Polynesian settlement
description: Voyagers from East Polynesia settle the last large habitable land on Earth; Wairau Bar is one of the oldest known villages.

title: Tasman reaches New Zealand
place: Off the West Coast, South Island
description: Abel Tasman's Dutch expedition makes the first known European sighting of the country, and four of his men are killed in a clash at Golden Bay five days later.

title: Cook lands at Poverty Bay
description: James Cook makes the first European landing and goes on to chart the whole coast in six months.

title: First Christian mission
description: Samuel Marsden preaches at the founding of the first mission station, the first lasting European settlement.

title: Declaration of Independence
description: Thirty-four northern chiefs declare the independence of their country under the name of the United Tribes of New Zealand.

title: Treaty of Waitangi
description: Māori chiefs and the British Crown sign the country's founding document, whose English and Māori texts differ on what was ceded.

title: Battle of Kororāreka
description: Hōne Heke cuts down the British flagstaff for the fourth time and the town is sacked, starting the first war between Māori and the Crown.

title: First Parliament meets
description: The General Assembly elected under the Constitution Act of 1852 opens, beginning self-government.

title: First Māori king
description: Pōtatau Te Wherowhero is made king by tribes seeking to unite and stop the sale of land.

title: Otago gold rush
description: Gabriel Read finds gold near Lawrence, and the rush that follows makes Dunedin the largest town in the country.

title: Invasion of the Waikato
description: British troops cross into the Māori king's territory, and after the war the government confiscates more than a million acres.

title: Capital moved to Wellington
description: Parliament moves from Auckland to a more central site on Cook Strait.

title: Invasion of Parihaka
description: About 1,600 armed constables and volunteers occupy a village that had led non-violent resistance to land confiscation, and arrest its leaders.

title: First frozen meat shipment
description: The ship Dunedin sails for London with a cargo of frozen mutton, opening the export trade on which the economy comes to rest.

title: Eruption of Mount Tarawera
description: The eruption kills about 120 people and destroys the Pink and White Terraces.

title: Women win the vote
description: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country in which women can vote in parliamentary elections.

title: Dominion status
description: The colony is proclaimed a dominion of the British Empire.

title: Hawke's Bay earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys much of Napier and Hastings and kills 256 people, the deadliest natural disaster in the country's history.

title: First Labour government elected
description: Labour under Michael Joseph Savage wins power and builds a welfare state with free health care and state housing.

title: Statute of Westminster adopted
description: Parliament adopts the statute of 1931, giving New Zealand full legal independence from Britain.

title: Waterfront dispute
description: A lockout of dock workers lasting 151 days, the largest industrial dispute in the country's history, ends in defeat for the unions.

title: Māori land march
description: A march led by Whina Cooper reaches Parliament from the far north, days after the Waitangi Tribunal is set up to hear claims under the treaty.

title: Springbok tour protests
description: A tour by the South African rugby team divides the country, and protesters force the cancellation of the match at Hamilton.

title: Sinking of the Rainbow Warrior
description: French agents bomb the Greenpeace ship in Auckland harbour, killing a photographer.

title: Nuclear-free law
description: Parliament bans nuclear weapons and nuclear-powered ships from the country, which costs it its place in the ANZUS alliance.

title: Vote for proportional representation
description: A referendum replaces first-past-the-post voting with a mixed-member proportional system.

title: Waikato-Tainui settlement
description: The Crown apologises for the invasion and confiscations of the 1860s and agrees the first large treaty settlement.

title: Christchurch earthquake
description: An earthquake under the city kills 185 people and wrecks the centre.

title: Christchurch mosque shootings
description: A gunman kills 51 people at two mosques, and Parliament bans most semi-automatic weapons within a month.
